Modeling Approach: Direct search (no MIP or QUBO model): minimum vertex cover local search, the stable set is the complement of the cover
Workflow: Greedy vertex cover, then NuMVC local search (Cai et al. 2013): two-stage exchange, edge weighting with forgetting (gamma = n/2, rho = 0.3), configuration checking; every cover found is recorded and one vertex removed to look for a smaller one; each run ends at its wall-clock limit; stable set = complement of the best cover, re-checked by an independent program.
Hardware Specifications: Apple M5 Pro (18 cores: 6 performance, 12 efficiency), 24 GB RAM, macOS 26.6.2; one single-threaded process per run at nice 10 on a machine shared with other jobs (load about 70-80)
Remarks: 30 s runs, seeds 1-5: Best stable set 58 over these 5 runs (listed best known 58: ours is equal to it). seed 1 (limit 30 s): 57, first reached at 1.5 s, run ended at 30.0 s wall / 12.5 s CPU; seed 2 (limit 30 s): 58, first reached at 16.8 s, run ended at 30.0 s wall / 12.5 s CPU; seed 3 (limit 30 s): 58, first reached at 12.1 s, run ended at 30.0 s wall / 12.6 s CPU; seed 4 (limit 30 s): 58, first reached at 4.1 s, run ended at 30.0 s wall / 12.5 s CPU; seed 5 (limit 30 s): 57, first reached at 2.5 s, run ended at 30.0 s wall / 12.6 s CPU. Total Runtime is the mean wall-clock time per run and CPU Runtime the mean process CPU time; the machine was shared, so a run waited for a free core part of the time and its CPU time is below its wall-clock time. Time to Solution is the mean wall-clock time at which each run first reached its own best. Optimality Bound N/A: the method computes no bound.
